subject: Nauru
note: Cited to one pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Nauru (revision 1385814755, which says the official English name became 'Republic of Naoero' in 2026; a script uses 'Nauru' and says Naoero is its name in Nauruan and now official). Figures used as stated: 21 km2, third-smallest country, about 12,000 people (third-smallest), the fringing reef, Command Ridge 71 m, about 80 per cent of the land stripped by mining, most people on the unmined coastal ring. NOT used: the 'about 30 km of road' (the page marks that sentence 'citation needed'), any driving time or circumference, the infobox density of 480 per km2 (it does not match 12,000 over 21 km2), and the Geography section's 'reef prevented a seaport' (the Transport section says Nauru has a port). Natural Earth's own area for Nauru (29 km2) differs from the page's 21 km2; the page's 21 km2 is the only area on screen. The marker is the page's infobox coordinate (0 deg 31' 39" S, 166 deg 56' 6" E). No old coastline is drawn.

claims.text: With an area of 21 km2, Nauru is the third-smallest country in the world, as well as the smallest member state of the Commonwealth of Nations by both area and population.
Its population of about 12,000 is the world's third-smallest (not including colonies or overseas territories).
Nauru is a 21 km2, oval-shaped island in the southwestern Pacific Ocean.
The island is surrounded by a fringing coral reef, which is exposed at low tide and dotted with pinnacles.
Coral cliffs surround a central plateau; the highest point of the plateau, Command Ridge, is 71 m above sea level.

Nauru is a phosphate-rock island, and most of its interior was strip-mined for about a century starting in 1900; mining has stripped and devastated about 80 per cent of Nauru's land area, leaving it uninhabitable.
The area where most Nauruans live now is the coastal ring of the island that has not been mined.
Nauru gained its independence from Australia in 1968.
Nauru's name in the Nauruan language is Naoero; in 2026 the official English name was changed to the Republic of Naoero.
